_doc: The town's script (townsfolk step 8, #1144; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5 'What they say'). The same shape as no_law.json (docs/scripts/README.md): `cast` the pools (townsfolk share pools by type, DESIGN §9; cast ids shared with no_law.json keep one voice), `scenes` with `lines` (id, speaker, trigger, when, condition, delivery, words, takes). Lines may hold slots in braces ({who}, {whom}, {where}, {shots}, {teller}); a scene's `reads` says which code reads it. The `runner` and `news` scenes are read by the game now (TownScript, src/people/town_script.gd; a wording `built` is what the game said before this file, kept); the rest wait for step 9's line picker. Every wording is PROPOSED and nothing is voiced until Sean taps Script OK. No line here says Harlan's name. No Law's town, morning and funeral lines stay in no_law.json and aren't repeated.

scenes.title: The news, as a man has it
scenes.when: Any day, the hours and the morning after a shooting
scenes.reads: TownNews.line_of (src/people/town_news.gd) builds a man's line from his own version: one head line by what he holds (a killing, a shooting, a man down, shots), then at most one of 'who drew first' or 'how many shots', then who told him. The most specific id with words first (news.killing.you, then news.killing); a wording by his seed, so three men who counted three shots say it three ways. Slots: {who} who fired (by TownNews.name_of: Earl, Cody, Doc, 'the new man' or 'the deputy', else 'the storekeeper'), {whom} who was hit ('a man' if he doesn't know), {where}, {shots} ('three shots'), {teller}. A sentence that starts with a slot gets its capital.
scenes.setting: A calm townsman near Harlan says his own news once, before his ordinary line; two townsmen telling each other say the same lines to each other. A version is only what that man sensed: a slot he didn't fill isn't spoken.

You hear? Last night.

That was you, shoving {whom} about, {at}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan shoved a man (#1272)

Saw you clean up at cards, {at}. Lucky hand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan took a pot at the card table (#1279)

That bluff of yours, {at}. Nothing but nerve.

lines.trigger: His version: Harlan's bluff at cards was shown up (#1279)

lines.trigger: His version: Harlan caught {whom} cheating at cards (#1279)

{who} called {whom} a cheat at cards, {at}, and he was one.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan called {whom} a cheat and he wasn't (#1279); {whom} is 'me' from the man called

Calling {whom} a cheat, {at}. Them's hard words, mister.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan called {whom} a cheat and it wasn't so (#1279)

words.text: {who} called {whom} a cheat at cards, {at}. Never proved a thing.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan stood the house a round (#1292)
lines.when: bar round; who Harlan; told to him

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan stood the house a round (#1292)

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan was drunk (#1292)
lines.when: bar drunk; who Harlan; told to him

You could hardly stand, {at}. I saw it.
{who} got good and drunk, {at}.
{who} was falling about drunk, {at}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: the deputy drinking on duty (#1292)
lines.when: bar deputy; who Harlan; told to him

words.text: You were drinking on duty, {at}. With that badge on.
Badge on and a glass in your hand, {at}. I saw.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: the deputy drinking on duty (#1292)

words.text: {who} was drinking on duty, {at}, badge and all.
{who} wears the badge and drinks on duty, {at}.

scenes.title: The morning after, about Harlan
scenes.when: The day after Harlan shot a man in town
scenes.reads: Step 9 (regard and the barks) picks these by StoryState news.harlan, set overnight by TownNews: stopped_a_killer (the man he shot fired first, or had shot someone), shot_a_man, split (near even). Said as Harlan passes, or to him; only by a man whose own version has Harlan in it.
scenes.setting: Main Street, the morning after. No line names him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: A touch of the hat; he isn't used to praising anybody.

words.text: Heard he pulled on you first. Nobody's grieving him.
Morning. That was a bad one you put down.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: Half to him, half to the woman beside her.

words.text: He'd shot one already, they say. Before you stopped him.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.delivery: Sets a glass down, and keeps his hand on the bottle.

words.text: This one's mine to stand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; his view shot_a_man (not to his face)
lines.delivery: Said once Harlan is past, loud enough.

words.text: That's him. Shot a man in the street.
Shot him before he'd cleared leather, I heard.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: To a boy at the window, not to Harlan.

words.text: Come away from there. Come inside.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Doesn't look up from the ledger.

words.text: I'll have the money first, if it's the same to you.
Depends who you ask. Some say the other fellow pulled first.
I heard it both ways. I don't know as I believe either.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; split; the loudmouth on the walk

words.text: I was told the fellow drew. Then I was told he never. Ask the deputy, he was stood right there, and I'd ask him myself only I'm busy.

scenes.title: The uneasy day
scenes.when: The day after a killing or a shooting the town holds (the calendar's `uneasy`)
scenes.reads: Step 9: barks by the day kind `uneasy` (valley_folk.json's kinds; StoryState news.yesterday = killing / shooting). Not after a story act's killing (No Law's morning is its own script).
scenes.setting: The storekeeper keeps in, the loudmouth's out on the walk telling it, the street's thinner.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Turning the sign, the bar in his other hand.

words.text: I'm barring the door tonight. You'd do the same.
Shutting early. It's nothing against you.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Wearing a pistol, at a lean spot

words.text: Never had cause to wear one in town before.
The wife made me put it on.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: On the walk, anyone within 4 m

words.text: Somebody ought to do something about it, and I said so, I said it to the storekeeper this morning.
I'd have stopped it, if I'd been there. I was at my supper.
You stay in the yard today, you hear me?
Nobody's out. Even the dogs are under the porch.

scenes.setting: The undertaker is exact; to him a dead man is a box, a name for the book and somebody to send the bill to.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.delivery: Already measuring him with his eye.

words.text: Stand away, please. Somebody take his feet.
I'll have him now. Mind his head on the step.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; his version has whom

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; nobody knows him

lines.speaker: undertaker

words.text: Yours, Deputy? I'll put it down that way.

scenes.when: Days after the cabin

scenes.when: Any day
scenes.reads: TownBarks `pass` (#1184): each man's own lines by his job (his pools), the hour and his spot, any regard but the cold and the afraid for the friendly ones; the gate's second round had one to four lines in ten minutes.
scenes.setting: Main Street by day.

words.text: Coffee's in. Flour's late. Same as every week.
Freight wagon's due Thursday, if the road holds.
Dust comes back faster than I can sweep it.
Mind the step. I've just wet it.
These crates don't get any lighter.
Nails, lamp oil, and a sack of something nobody ordered.
Slow today. Folks are keeping their money in their boots.
If you're buying, I'm selling. If you're looking, look quick.
Near closing. Whatever you want, want it now.
Shutting up shop directly.
Grey mare threw a shoe again. Smith'll love that.
Morning. Hay's gone up a nickel.
Horses have more sense than half this town.
That bay's been kicking the boards all day. Don't stand behind him.
Feed and a stall, two bits a night. Less if you muck it yourself.
Wind's got the horses jumpy.
Stand off the anvil. I don't want to burn you.
Iron's the only thing in this town that does what it's told.
Fire's lit before the rooster. Every day.
Morning. Bring me anything bent and I'll make it straight.
Livery owes me for four shoes. Don't tell him I said.
Hands like these, and they want me to write my name neat.
Keep your feet dry and your powder drier.
Nobody's sick today. I don't trust it.
Morning. If you're bleeding, come by. If you're not, good.
Morning. Sleep, if you can get it. Best medicine I've got.

lines.trigger: You pass him in the street

words.text: Forgive me. I measure folk by eye. Habit.
Quiet week. Good news for everybody but me.
Don't suppose there's any work in this town.
I've seen worse towns. Not many.
Just holding up the wall. It'd fall without me.
Sun's warm. Wall's warm. I'm not moving.
Boots off my rug. I mean it.
Rooms are fifty cents. Clean sheets are extra, and worth it.
I've two rooms empty, if you know anybody respectable.
Supper's at six. Late is cold.
Too early for the piano. Too late for church.
You're not buying, you're just looking. I know the type.
It's quiet till sundown. Then it's not.
Buy a girl a sarsaparilla? No? Suit yourself.
Bar's open. Whiskey's two bits, and it isn't worth it.
Glasses don't clean themselves. More's the pity.
This town's dead as a doornail till payday.
I could lift that wagon. Bet me a dollar.
Hot as the hinges out here. Somebody stand me a beer.
Noon, and not a drop taken. A man could die.
Best seat in town. Free, too.
Sit down, sit down. The bench don't bite.
Dry as a bone. We could use a rain.
Looks like weather out west.
Morning.
Mm. Morning.

lines.speaker: townsman

words.text: Dinner bell's gone. Too hot to eat.
Sun's straight up. Not a lick of shade.
Half the town's at its dinner. The other half wants to be.

words.text: Long afternoon.
Same as yesterday. Hotter.
Evening.
Getting on for supper.
Sit if you like. Bench don't belong to me.
I'm resting my feet. They've earned it.
Can't stop. I'm behind already.
Busy. Talk later.
Waiting on the mail. It's always late.
Just seeing who's about.
Morning. Mind the mud by the trough.
Morning. You're up early.
Don't block the walk, please.
Have you seen what they want for sugar?
Evening to you.
It gets dark earlier every night.

scenes.when: Any day, two men within a few metres of each other

words.text: Flour's up again. Robbery, plain and simple.
You seen the price of coffee? I'll drink water.
Rain by Sunday. You mark me.
Creek's lower than I've ever seen it.
Railroad man was in again, asking after land.
They say the line's coming through north of the creek.
Baron's men moved a herd past the creek last night.
Saw dust on the east road. Cattle, a lot of 'em.
My wife says I talk too much. I told her she don't listen.
Wife's sister's coming. For a month.
Lost four dollars to Earl last night. Four!
That drifter plays cards like he's got nowhere to be.
They say the mine's hiring again.
Miner come in with a poke of dust yesterday. Spent it all by dark.
Stage brought no mail again. Three weeks.
Letter come for the widow Pratt. Nobody wants to take it up.
Preacher's coming through next month, if he don't get lost again.
Church roof wants fixing before the snow.
Your account's at nine dollars. I'm only saying.
Got a bolt of blue calico in. Pretty, if you like blue.
Bring it round after dinner and I'll true it up.
That wheel's got a cracked felloe. It'll go on you.
Feed bill's due. I'm not a charity.
Your horse ate more'n you did this week.
I'll tell you what this town needs. A second saloon.
I arm-wrestled a mule skinner in Abilene. Beat him twice.
The Pratt girl's walking out with the bank clerk.
I'd not let a daughter of mine near that saloon.
Hens have stopped laying. It's the heat.
Did you hear the dog howling half the night?

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: To a man at his bar

words.text: Beer's warm. Ice wagon never came.
Swept this floor twice today and it's still dirty.
That cough of yours wants listening to. Come by.
Eat something green once a week. That's all I ask.
The piano man's sweet on the landlady. Don't say I told you.
Earl tipped me a whole dollar last night. Then asked for it back.
Your room's paid to Friday. After that, we'll see.
The drummer in number four snores like a sawmill.
Rode in from Tascosa. Nothing there either.
I'll take any work going. Fences, horses, anything.
That so.
Is that right.
Hm. Could be.
Might be, might be.
Don't I know it.
You're telling me.
You don't say.
Well, I'll be.
Ha! That'll be the day.
Ha. Pull the other one.
Could be worse.
Been worse.
I heard different.
That's not how I heard it.
Well. What can you do.
Nothing to be done about it.
True enough.
Can't argue with that.
Tell me later. I've work.
Not now, I'm busy.
Well, I never.
Goodness.
I'm sure I don't know.
Hmph. Men.

scenes.title: Overheard at the saloon's bar
scenes.when: With you in hearing; each exchange by its own `when`
scenes.reads: Overheard (src/people/overheard.gd, #1293): the lines that share an `ex` are one exchange, said in this order by `who` to `to`, when its cast stand together at spots tagged `place` and its first line's `if` holds. One wording a line: each answers the last.
scenes.setting: The saloon: at the bar

words.text: Same again, my son. It do lay the dust.
That's your fourth, Jory.
Is it? I'd lost the count. Go on, then.
Ground's talking in the east drift again. All night shift she were at it.
Talking how?
Little cracks. Like a man's knuckles. Timber man says 'tis only settling.
Well. He'd know, I guess.
He goes up to grass at ten every morning. I couldn't tell 'ee what he knows.
God damn it, Rufe, set it down like you paid for it!
I did pay for it!
You paid for the whiskey. Them glasses come up from Denver in straw, and half of 'em don't come.
I've throwed better glasses than that at a mule! In Santa Fe, this was, the mule had got into...
Thirty-one dollars, Rufe.
Fellow got down off the noon train with a saddle and no trunk. That's worth a short one.
What kind of saddle?
Texas rig, double cinch. Went up to the hotel and never looked at nobody.
Who'd he ask for?
I never followed him in! I got freight to carry, I can't be following every man with a saddle!
One. And I'll be slow with it, if you don't mind.
You're an hour over every one, Don Anselmo. I could have had three men at that piece of rail.
It's dark past the ford, and that horse don't like the ford. I wait for the moon.
That's your grass the Baron's wire goes round, down by the ford?
It was mine. I sold him the low meadow in 'seventy-six. He paid what I asked, in gold, the same day.
Then you've no quarrel with him.
No. Only the creek below it, it used to come up to my knee. Now it's here. My ankle.
That's the dry years, maybe.
Hey! Hey, Mexican! What's wool fetching?
Twenty-two cents. My name is Gallegos, Mr. Mapes.
I hear a heap of things. I disremember the most of 'em.
Rufe.
What? I only asked the man about wool!
That's a churchyard cough, Jory.
'Tis powder smoke. Comes up of a morning and then I'm right.
I had a faro dealer told me that. We put him up the hill inside the year.
Did he work powder?
He dealt faro, Jory. I just told you.
Letter goes Thursday. Four pound in it, if the cards leave me be.
To your wife.
Loveday, and the maid. Maid were six when I come away. She's seventeen now, and writes a better hand than her mother.
That's a long time, to send letters.
One more year, I told her. I've told her that in... well. In a good few letters.
One whiskey. It's eight by your clock.
Ten past, Mr. Colby.
Is it. I was planing and lost the light. There's a lid to fit yet tonight.
Who for?
Nobody you know. A section hand, off the cars. The depot can't tell me his name.
What're you looking at, Colby?
Was I? I beg your pardon, Mr. Mapes. I was a long way off.
I ain't sick!
I never said you were.
You seen him, Jory. He was looking right at me. I don't care for it, a man in that trade.
I've wrote to Kansas City again for black walnut. Seasoned.
Who's it for?
Whoever asks. Nobody has, in five years. They take the pine.
What's the difference to a man?
Forty-odd dollars. And walnut takes a polish.
He's had six and he's showing me a picture of his mother.
He's bought six. I don't see what you got to grieve over.
She's a hard-looking woman, is what. And he wants me to say she's not.
Fellow by the window's got nobody with him.
I saw him. Let me stand here a while first.
Hold eight back for the first. Same as always.
Eight. Pueblo again?
It's wrote in your book where it goes. You needn't say it out across the bar.
I never said a thing but the town.
Stand me one, Jory, and I'll tell you what Hollis's wife said about the widow Rudd.
I board with the widow Rudd.
Well, that's how come you'd want to know!
She keeps my bed when I'm short. I'll hear nothing, Rufe.
Twelve yoke I had. Twelve! Over Mosquito Pass in the snow, and never lost a sack.
And where be they now?
Butcher's got the last of 'em. Railroad done that. I went down to the agent and I told him what I thought of his cars, to his face!
What'd he say to that?
He never heard me. He was inside.
Mine paid at noon?
Noon. Money order's put by, and Mrs. Rudd had hers off me at the door.
And the rest?
The rest is here. Pour, and don't look so glad about it.
They docked you for candles again! I wouldn't stand for it, not me!
You'd say it from grass, my son. We buy our candles and we buy our powder. Always did.
That's robbery!
Like enough. It's three dollars a day after, and there's Loveday to send to.
Preacher's gone by twice. Slow, both times.
He's counting your shutters.
Eleven. He can count till dark, they're paid for.
Church has the one. I've seen it bang, in a wind.

words.text: That'll do no harm, will it? Pour it.
Creek's down again. My well's fourteen foot to water, and it was ten.
My acequia's a hand deep at noon. When I was a boy it was over my head. We lost my brother in it.
Drowned?
He was eight. I was up with the sheep, I didn't see it.
Wool's twenty-two cents at Pueblo. Last year, twenty-eight.
Whiskey's up a dollar ten the barrel since the cars. They told me the cars'd bring it down.
They told me the same about freight on wool. The agent, he had a paper with it printed.
They all got a paper.
My younger boy wants to go on the railroad. A brakeman.
How old is he?
Nineteen. Eusebio.
I were five year under ground by that. You'll not keep him, if he's set.
No. His mother thinks I can. She has me talk to him every Sunday, and he listens, he's a good boy. And Monday he's down at the depot again.
My pistol, please. I'm going.
Cap and ball. That's an old one. You ever fire it?
At a coyote, in the spring. He was among the lambs.
Get him?
I don't think so. He ran, anyway, and I had the lamb.
There's the whistle. Night shift's going down, and my bed's empty for the first time since morning.
You share a bed?
Share it! We never met. He's in it days and I'm in it nights. I know him by his boots under it.
She charge the both of you?
She do.
This one's thin, my son.
It's the same barrel as yesterday.
I thought yesterday's were thin.
Somebody's been at it with a dipper, then, and by God it ain't me. I'll sleep down here tonight.
That's the last on the slate, Rufe.
Then I'll take my trade down to the Railroad Saloon!
Go on. They want cash down there, same as me.
They got forty-rod at a nickel!
So you tell me, every time. Mind the step.
Kitty! Come sit by a man that's been somewhere.
It's four bits, Rufe. Have you got it?
Put it on the slate!
Ask himself, so. I'll wait here while you do.
You'd not buy a lady a drink, Jory?
'Tis cold tea, maid. I've watched him pour it.
It is, and he gets three parts of the money.
Then here. That's for you. Put it away before he looks round.
Don Anselmo. You'll want nothing from me, same as ever.
No, thank you. You look tired, Miss Kitty.
My feet aren't. The rest of me's grand.
My wife puts hers in the ditch, at shearing. She says it's the cold does it. I don't know, you have no ditch here.
Company mules used to water at the spring below the dump. There's posts round it now.
Cedar posts. I saw them, coming in.
So now they haul it up from the creek, two barrels a day.
Whose posts?
Nobody at the office will say.
Professor wants a tuner up from Denver. Twelve dollars and his fare.
The C sticks. I've heard it stick.
I can't hear it. Can you hear it over them boots?
Chapel at St Just had a harmonium with three dead. We sang round 'em.
Preacher says you carried his stove up the lane on your back.
Who says?
He do. Says you took nothing for it.
It wasn't heavy. And don't you go telling that round, I got a name in this town.

words.text: Well, a man can see from behind a trough!
You sitting in Friday?
I always sit in Friday.
Earl takes a dollar off you every time he deals.
He do. I watch for how. Three year, and I've not caught him at it yet.
You drinking, Wiley, or leaning?
I got a nickel. I was working up to it.
Work up to it off the varnish. That top come from St. Louis.
Beer, then. Slow as you like.
You wouldn't want a lot? Fifty feet on Main. The west end.
Depot's at the east end, Mr. Peck.
The company may yet see reason. I calculate... a siding, at the least.
What'd you give for 'em?
I'd as soon not say it in here.
I carried nine loads for Hollis this week and he paid me for seven!
So you got seven loads' pay on you.

He did. He did do that. ...I ain't saying the cars is all bad.

Put me down. I never in my life.
Four shoes I owe Stroud for. Since August.

I mean to pay him! That ain't what I'm telling you.
I added the book again this evening.
Quit adding it.
The single men pay. It's the ones with families run behind, and I can't... there's a woman comes in for cornmeal, Hiram.
Then you'll carry her, same as last winter. Drink that.
You bar up before you come over?
Lavinia drops it behind me. I knock three and one and she lifts it.
Three and one.
Don't say it over, Hiram.
Mr. Hollis. Your wife sold me a card of buttons today and never once looked at me.
She... I'm sure she meant nothing by it.
Ah, she did. It's no matter, Mr. Hollis, I've the buttons.

Ranch crowd rode in six strong today and tied at the rail. Not a nickel's hay amongst 'em.

What'd they buy?
Goods.
What goods?
I'd as soon not, Hiram. How's the roan?
That's half past nine.
It's twenty past.
She'll be listening for me.
Go on, then. Mind the hole by the trough, I near went in it.
Watch the Professor when I say 'Mrs. Rudd'. ...There. Did you hear that?
He's dropped a note.
He mends her organ Sundays and eats in the kitchen for it.
That's nobody's business but theirs.
Ah, sure. I wouldn't say it to him.
Two tonight?
It's payday. The mine's men paid down sixty-three dollars on the book since dinner.
Every horse I own went out this morning. I ain't been round the stalls yet to see what come back.
Have the second one first.
Mapes laid a whip on a team outside my door today. Hired team.
He carries my freight.
I know whose freight he carries. That near mule won't stand to be harnessed now for a week. I'll be the one gets kicked.
